identity.name: Akira (Howling Scorpius) vCenter-to-ESXi Kill Chain — VMDK-Copy Offline Credential Theft to Akira_v2 Encryption (SIM-EDR-019)
identity.summary: Howling Scorpius pivots from a compromised vCenter into the ESXi hypervisor plane: it powers off the Domain Controller VM, clones the DC VMDK to an attacker VM to extract NTDS.dit + SYSTEM hive OFFLINE (bypassing on-host EDR entirely), redirects ESXi syslog to /tmp to blind the host, mass powers-off every guest via vim-cmd getallvms, and detonates the Rust Akira_v2 encryptor (--vmonly).
identity.description: Models the novel hypervisor kill chain from Unit 42's Howling Scorpius (Akira) threat assessment. The defensive point of this card is causality ownership: the Causality Group Owner is the ESXi shell (esxcli / vim-cmd) reached from a vCenter-initiated session — NOT the CortexSim beacon — and the whole chain (DC power-off -> VMDK clone -> offline credential theft on the cloned disk -> syslog blinding -> mass power-off -> Akira_v2 encryption) stitches into ONE incident on the causality_actor_process_* instance. The offline-VMDK credential-theft step is the differentiator: because the credentials are dumped from a cloned disk on the attacker's VM, an endpoint-only detection on the real DC never fires — Cortex catches it through the hypervisor process lineage + the cloned-VMDK shared entity instead.

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-EDR-019 — Akira Howling Scorpius vCenter-to-ESXi hypervisor kill chain (Unit 42).

prerequisites.description: Cortex XDR / XSIAM agent installed on the ESXi/Linux target so per-process causality telemetry reaches xdr_data.

payload.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# SAFE-MODE: non-destructive simulation of the Akira Howling Scorpius
# vCenter-to-ESXi kill chain. Every hypervisor action is echoed with a
# SAFE-MODE marker; no VM is powered off, no disk is cloned, nothing is
# encrypted. The value is the process-causality telemetry, not real impact.
set -euo pipefail
MARK='[CortexSim SAFE-MODE SIM-EDR-019]'
DC_VMID='42'
DATASTORE='/vmfs/volumes/datastore1'

echo "${MARK} step-01 ESXi shell established from vCenter session (CGO=esxcli)"
esxcli --version 2>/dev/null || echo "${MARK} esxcli not present (simulated)"

echo "${MARK} step-02 power off DC VM (vim-cmd vmsvc/power.off ${DC_VMID})"
echo "${MARK} SAFE-MODE would run: vim-cmd vmsvc/power.off ${DC_VMID}"

echo "${MARK} step-03 clone DC VMDK to attacker VM folder"
echo "${MARK} SAFE-MODE would run: vmkfstools -i ${DATASTORE}/DC/DC.vmdk ${DATASTORE}/attacker/dc-clone.vmdk"

echo "${MARK} step-04 offline NTDS.dit + SYSTEM hive extraction on cloned disk"
echo "${MARK} SAFE-MODE would run: secretsdump.py -ntds ntds.dit -system SYSTEM LOCAL"

echo "${MARK} step-05 blind ESXi syslog (esxcli system syslog config set --logdir=/tmp)"
echo "${MARK} SAFE-MODE would run: esxcli system syslog config set --logdir=/tmp"

echo "${MARK} step-06 mass power-off all guests (vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms | power.off)"
echo "${MARK} SAFE-MODE would run: vim-cmd vmsvc/getallvms | awk power.off fan-out"

echo "${MARK} step-07 detonate Akira_v2 --vmonly (encrypt .vmdk/.vmx datastore files)"
echo "${MARK} SAFE-MODE would run: ./akira --id <key> --vmonly --stopvm"
echo "${MARK} SIM-EDR-019 simulation complete (no destructive action taken)"

input_variables.description: vim-cmd vmsvc id of the Domain Controller VM the chain targets (simulation only).

input_variables.name: DATASTORE
input_variables.description: ESXi datastore path the cloned VMDK and encryption markers reference (simulation only).

biocs.name: Akira ESXi Interactive Shell From vCenter-Initiated Session
biocs.description: The Causality Group Owner: an esxcli/vim-cmd shell whose causality actor is a vCenter-initiated sshd/hostd/dcui session. Keys on causality_actor_process_* + instance_id so every downstream hypervisor action is owned by this CGO rather than the beacon.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter action_process_image_name in ("esxcli", "vim-cmd", "localcli")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("sshd", "hostd", "dcui")
| comp count() as shell_execs by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id
| filter shell_execs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, shell_execs

biocs.name: Akira v2 VM-Only Encryption Impact on ESXi Datastore
biocs.description: Burst of file creations with the .akiranew extension or the akiranew.txt ransom note under /vmfs/volumes/ — the Akira_v2 --vmonly encryption impact stage.
biocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type = ENUM.FILE_CREATE
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter action_file_path starts_with "/vmfs/volumes/"
| filter action_file_extension = "akiranew" or action_file_name = "akiranew.txt"
| bin _time span=5m
| comp count() as impacted_files by agent_hostname, action_file_extension, _time
| filter impacted_files >= 5
| fields agent_hostname, action_file_extension, impacted_files, _time

xql_queries.name: Confirm ESXi DC-VM Power-Off and VMDK Copy Sequence

abiocs.name: Akira ESXi Offline VMDK Credential-Theft Pivot
abiocs.description: The novel differentiator: after the DC VMDK is cloned, an offline extractor (mimikatz/secretsdump/esentutl/reg) reads NTDS.dit + SYSTEM/SAM from the mounted clone on the attacker VM. Because the dump happens off-host, no endpoint detection fires on the real DC — the ABIOC anchors on the cloned-VMDK shared entity crossing into the attacker VM's process lineage.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("mimikatz.exe", "secretsdump.py", "impacket-secretsdump", "esentutl.exe", "reg.exe")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains "ntds" or action_process_image_command_line contains "NTDS" or action_process_image_command_line contains "SYSTEM" or action_process_image_command_line contains "SAM"
| comp count() as offline_extractions by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_instance_id
| filter offline_extractions >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, causality_actor_process_instance_id, actor_process_instance_id, offline_extractions
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned baseline where DC credential material never leaves the DC endpoint -> deviation: NTDS.dit/SYSTEM-hive access originates from an attacker VM reading a cloned DC VMDK, anchored to the cloned-disk shared entity rather than to the DC's own process tree.

abiocs.name: Akira ESXi Mass Guest Power-Off Fan-Out From Blinded Host
abiocs.description: A single ESXi shell lineage that powers off an anomalously high number of guest VMs via vim-cmd getallvms|power.off, diverging from the host's learned admin power-cycle baseline — the pre-encryption mass shutdown.
abiocs.logic:
preset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter action_process_image_name = "vim-cmd" and action_process_image_command_line contains "power.off"
| comp count() as guests_powered_off by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name
| filter guests_powered_off >= 10
| sort desc guests_powered_off
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_instance_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, guests_powered_off
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-host baseline of concurrent guest power-off operations under a single ESXi shell instance -> deviation: dozens of power.off calls from one causality_actor_process_instance_id within minutes, immediately after syslog redirection.

threat_steps.objective: The ESXi process lineage (shell -> DC power-off -> VMDK clone -> mass power-off) is owned by the vCenter-initiated CGO, not the beacon.
preconditions: Cortex agent installed on the ESXi/Linux target.
steps: Open the causality view for the esxcli/vim-cmd CGO.
success_criteria: BIOC `Akira ESXi Interactive Shell From vCenter-Initiated Session` fires and the DC power-off + VMDK clone events share its causality_actor_process_instance_id.

threat_steps.objective: The offline VMDK credential-theft pivot is detected via the cloned-disk shared entity despite no endpoint dump on the real DC.
preconditions: Cortex agent on the attacker VM reading the cloned VMDK.
success_criteria: ABIOC `Akira ESXi Offline VMDK Credential-Theft Pivot` raises on the offline NTDS/SYSTEM-hive access.

threat_steps.objective: The full chain auto-promotes to one P1 incident.
preconditions: All simulation steps executed within the correlation window.
success_criteria: Correlation `CR-EDR-0019` stitches all five signals into a single hypervisor-ransomware incident.

preventive_controls: Enforce MFA and just-in-time access on vCenter/ESXi management interfaces; disable ESXi Shell and SSH except during change windows.
Ship ESXi syslog to a remote collector and alert on any local syslog-directory reconfiguration.
Restrict datastore browser and vmkfstools/VMDK-copy operations to a break-glass admin group; monitor VMDK clones to non-standard paths.
Isolate the vCenter management network and keep Domain Controllers off shared datastores accessible to general-purpose VMs.
detection_engineering: Alert on esxcli `system syslog config set --logdir=/tmp` and any syslog reload that shortens retention.
Baseline concurrent vim-cmd power.off volume per ESXi host and fire on fan-out above the learned admin baseline.
Correlate DC-VM power-off -> VMDK clone -> offline NTDS/SYSTEM access on the cloned disk as one causality chain, keyed on causality_actor_process_instance_id and the cloned-VMDK entity.
